about.title: Oakdale Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Stanislaus County's crash records show Oakdale sees dozens of injury collisions each year, concentrated around corridors like E F Street, W F Street, and Rt 108, with Friday midday hours showing more reported crashes than other times. While recent final figures show no traffic deaths recorded that year, fatal outcomes from vehicle crashes and other preventable incidents still happen in communities like Oakdale, and they leave families facing grief alongside financial strain. California law gives certain surviving family members the right to pursue a wrongful death claim, separate from any criminal proceedings against the person responsible. Our team handles wrongful death claims directly and can explain standing, deadlines, and what losses may be recoverable. There's no fee unless we recover something on your behalf.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before Pursuing a Wrongful Death Claim

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits who has standing to bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and extending to certain dependents or other heirs if none of those exist. We can clarify where your family stands before any paperwork begins.

items.title: The Clock Is Shorter Than Many Expect
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim in California, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Waiting to sort through grief is understandable, but it can also cost your family the ability to file at all.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Funeral Costs
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial expenses, the financial support a loved one would have provided, and compensation for the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. We can help identify which losses apply to your specific circumstances.

items.question: Does the wrongful death case depend on whether there's a criminal case too?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal prosecution the driver or responsible party might face. Even if criminal charges are never filed, or the outcome doesn't go the way you'd hope, your family may still be able to pursue a civil claim.

items.question: Oakdale's most recent crash data shows zero traffic deaths that year. Does that mean wrongful death claims don't apply here?
items.answer: That count reflects one specific year of traffic-related fatalities, and it doesn't rule out other years or other causes like premises incidents or defective products. If your family has lost someone under circumstances that seem preventable, it's worth having us review what happened, regardless of citywide statistics.

items.question: What if my loved one wasn't married and didn't have children?
items.answer: California's wrongful death law still allows for other dependents or heirs to potentially bring a claim when there's no surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. This can get complicated depending on your family's specific situation, so it helps to talk it through with us and review the details.
